why: the refusal has to name the map's version and the bound it crossed - here the ceiling, because the document is from after this library; the too-old case names the floor instead, and a single message about the range 1 through 2 satisfies neither and fails this `match`. An earlier Python message rendered a literal '{CONTRACT}' here while TypeScript rendered the number, which is a divergence no vector reached: the suite compared encodings and this path produces only a diagnostic. The map declared 2 until contract 2 shipped, at which point the shape it refused became a valid one - so it declares 3 now. That edit is a contract change and section 11 asks for it to be deliberate, which is what this sentence is. A version above the ceiling is refused because what came after this library cannot be known; one below it is accepted, which every other map vector here exercises by declaring 1. The number in this case moves with the ceiling: it declared 3 against a library that implemented 2, and on 7 September 2026 the map contract went to 3 because equalising the ClickHouse timestamp precision changed which `also_write` maps a library accepts - a loosening, which §11 says bumps. So the case now declares 4. What it pins is not a particular number but the direction: forwards is strict, because what came after cannot be known.
